Hi, Rafael, it is Claire. Before tomorrow's meeting, I want to be honest with you. My client likes the deal, but the price is a problem. If you lowered it by ten percent, I think we would sign tomorrow. We could also be flexible on the payment. For example, we could pay forty percent upfront and the rest in twelve months. The delivery date is not a deal-breaker for us. Please think about it, and call me tonight if you can.

I have closed more than two hundred deals, and the last meeting always feels the same. Everybody is tired, and everybody wants to finish. My advice is simple. Before the meeting, write your bottom line on a piece of paper, and do not change it in the room. If the other side asks for a concession, ask for one back. And remember that walking away is also a result. If I had to choose between a bad deal and no deal, I would choose no deal every time. But most of the time, if both sides meet halfway, the deal closes, and everybody goes home happy.

First, thank the other side and confirm the main points. Then, say your bottom line. Next, make an offer with if and would. After that, meet halfway on the small problems. Finally, put everything in a term sheet and close the deal.
